case_name: Rohit Kaushal & Anr. vs State & Ors.
facts_of_case: Petitioner No.2 left her parents' house without pressure or coercion from Petitioner No.1. She claims to have married him and saptpadi was performed. FIR registered under Section 363 of IPC by father of Petitioner No.2.

legal_principles.principle: If a minor does not raise an alarm or put up a struggle when leaving her guardian's custody, it is difficult to accept that she did so voluntarily.
legal_principles.held: The Hon'ble Supreme Court noted that it was not unknown to her with whom she was going and therefore, it was expected of her then to jump down from the bicycle or put up the struggle and in any case raise an alarm to protect herself.
cited_cases: Shyam & Another Vs. State of Maharashtra, (1995) Criminal Law General 3974
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — highlights the importance of a minor's actions in determining their voluntary departure from custody

legal_principles.principle: In cases where a minor goes with someone voluntarily, it is difficult to hold that the accused took her away from the keeping of her lawful guardian.
legal_principles.held: It was held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that the requirement of Section 366 of IPC is that taking or enticing away a minor out of the keeping of the lawful guardianship was an essential ingredient of the offence of kidnapping.
cited_cases: State of Karnataka vs. Sureshbabu, (1994) Crl.L.J.1216(1)
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — highlights the importance of a minor's actions in determining whether an accused has taken them away from their lawful guardian

outcome.final_order: No offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC will be made out when the girl is aged more than 16 years and is mature enough to understand what she is doing.

use_for_drafting: advising on marriage and family law
